newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Pick 'n Pay in JV with S.Africa's 7-Eleven.
newsitem.headline: Pick 'n Pay in JV with S.Africa's 7-Eleven.

text.p: Pick 'n Pay Stores Ltd said on Tuesday it had formed a joint venture company with Cape-based retailer 7-Eleven Stores to facilitate rapid new convenience store developments outside the Western Cape province.
It said in a statement the new joint venture firm, called 7-Eleven Africa Ltd, would be 60 percent owned by Pick 'n Pay, which would also run the venture, and 40 percent by 7-Eleven.

The first new stores to be opened under the joint venture umbrella would be in the most populous Gauteng province. Two Pick 'n Pay-owned SA Cafe stores would be converted into pilot stores to gauge buying patterns and community acceptance.
"We plan to open at least 20 new 7-Eleven convenience stores in Gauteng in our first year of operation," said Gareth Ackerman, managing director of Pick 'n Pay group enterprises.
"Our expansion, while limited to Gauteng in the short term, will certainly be extended to other provinces in the near future," he said.
Some stores would be owned directly by 7-Eleven Africa Ltd but it was intended that all future stores would ultimately be franchised.

The agreement does not affect existing 7-Eleven stores in the Western Cape. These stores, together with 7-Eleven owner George Hadjidakis, would provide regular advice and input to Pick 'n Pay on the running of the new venture.
7-Eleven, which had a turnover of 250 million rand in 1996, runs 120 stores -- a sizeable percentage of which are franchised, with the remainder being corporate owned.

Ackerman said the joint venture added impetus to the group's efforts to enter the fuel industry. Pick 'n Pay has long argued against price controls regulating South Africa's liquid fuels industry, believing it can offer better value to consumers by selling supermarket branded products through "no-frills" self-service stations.
